subject: island airport
title: What If an Airport Sank Into the Sea? Japan's Is, 38 Feet So Far

scenes.text: What if an airport was sinking into the sea? Japan's is, 38 feet so far.
It opened in 1994 on an artificial island three miles out in Osaka Bay, built from more than 200 million cubic metres of fill.
Engineers expected the soft clay seabed to settle. The first island sank 27 feet before opening day, not the 19 predicted.
The terminal sits on 900 columns resting on hydraulic jacks, adjusted to keep the floor level as the ground drops.
Over 150 million dollars went into raising the seawall. In 2018, Typhoon Jebi overtopped it anyway, flooding the runway and stranding 5,000 people.
Sinking has slowed to about 6 centimetres a year. Still, some engineers warn parts of the islands could reach sea level around 2056.

description:
What if an airport sank into the sea? Kansai International, opened in 1994 on an artificial island in Osaka Bay, has sunk about 38 feet since opening as the clay seabed compresses; the first island settled 27 feet before opening day against a prediction of 19.
The terminal rests on 900 adjustable hydraulic jacks, more than 150 million dollars has gone into raising the seawall, and Typhoon Jebi still flooded the runway in 2018. Subsidence is now about 6 centimetres a year, but some engineers warn parts could reach sea level around 2056.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Kansai still handled over 30 million passengers in 2024 while sinking. Which engineering gamble should we run through next?
